summary: Jules Brooks Levinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia in 1994 under Jeffrey Hopkins and studied with several traditional teachers. In 1996, he was an assistant professor at Hamline University.

Jules Luquiens (1845–1899) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at the University of Geneva and Yale University under William Dwight Whitney, he taught French at Cincinnati and MIT, then served as Professor of Modern Languages at Yale (1892–1899).

Jules Marouzeau (1878–1964) was a French linguist who studied at the Sorbonne under Antoine Meillet. He served as Directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 1920 and as Professor of Latin at the Sorbonne from 1925 to 1948.

Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was a French historian educated at Lycée Charlemagne. He held teaching posts at the École Normale Supérieure, served as a section chief at the Archives nationales (1830–1851), and was Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Jules Oppert (1825–1905) was a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Berlin, and Kiel, and served as professor at the INALCO, the Bibliothèque nationale de France, and the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Jules Pierre Barthoux (1881–1965) was an archaeologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing his doctoral degree at the University of Lille in 1922, he headed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan from 1923 to 1933.

Jules Thonnelier (d. 1879) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He was a member of the Société Asiatique from approximately 1854 to 1879 and the Société de l'histoire de France from around 1860 to 1879.

Julia A. B. Hegewald (born 1971) is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (BA and PhD), the University of Oxford (MA), and completed her Habilitation at RWTH Aachen University.

Julia Ching (1934–2001) worked in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy, completing degrees at the Catholic University of America and the Australian National University. She taught at Columbia and Yale before becoming a professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

Julia F. Andrews (born 1951) is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Brown University, Harvard University, and the University of California, Berkeley, and joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.

Julia König specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a Magister Artium at the University of Jena (2006–2013), where she also held a post in the Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences from 2008 to 2009.

Julia Leslie (1948–2004) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Sussex and the University of Oxford, she served as Lecturer and later Reader in Hindu Studies at SOAS University of London from 1990 to 2004.
Julian Schott is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He is attested in 2026 as a faculty member at the University of Vienna and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Juliane Schober is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989. She served as an associate professor of religious studies at Arizona State University, attested in 1997 and 2007.

Julie Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Chicago under the supervision of Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University in 2011.

Julien Girard de Rialle (1841–1904) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes under Honoré-Joseph Chavée and served as a lecturer at the Sorbonne.

Julien Levesque is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Sciences Po, Columbia, and the EHESS, he has held posts at the Centre de Sciences Humaines, Ashoka University, the University of Zurich, and the CNRS.

Julien Vinson (1843–1926) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the École Nationale du Génie Rural, des Eaux et des Forêts. From 1879 to 1921, he served as Professor of Hindustani and Tamil at the INALCO.

Julieta Rotaru is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Bucharest and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth. She held posts at the University of Bucharest, Bucharest Metropolitan Library, Södertörn University, and INALCO.

Julius Dutoit (1872–1958) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Giessen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg under Adalbert Kuhn and Ernst Kuhn. He served as director of the Riemenschneider-Gymnasium from 1929 to 1934.
